newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end down, traders await govt package.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end down, traders await govt package.

text.p: Blue chips suffered fresh losses in jittery trade on Thursday triggered by speculation about much-awaited policy measures due this week, dealers said.
"Trading was very volatile. People who were hopeful about government announcements are suddenly turning a little less upbeat" said Hiren Ved, an equities analyst at Prime Securities.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) ended 16.99 points lower to provisional 3,508.98.

Market regulator, the Securities & Exchange Board of India, (SEBI) is scheduled to hold a new conference at 5.30 p.m. (local) which follows a day-long meeting that will deliberate a new takeover code, stock lending scheme, amendment in the share depository act and a report on short sales, an official said.
"There was a lack of direction for market players...they didn't know what to do..." Prime's Ved said.
Among other things, traders are hoping for tax breaks on company dividends, easing of carry-forward rules for stock markets and a buy-back of shares.
High expectations about market-friendly initiatives promised by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda have led Indian stocks to rally nearly 24 percent in less than a month.
"There is definitely some nervousness...A lot of people have built up positions on high expectations," said Prashant Purker, head of sales at Peregrine Capital. "This market is of hopes and fears..."
Earlier this week, Deve Gowda had said the government would announce new economic measures before he leaves for the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, on Friday.
"Quite frankly, the situation is very fluid," M.G. Damani, the Bombay Stock Exchange president told Reuters. "The government will have to face the music if the market slumps."
The government on Thursday said it will treat telecom companies as infrastructure firms and offer them a five-year tax holiday and import duty concessions.
Among pivotal stocks, SBI rose 1.25 rupees to 293.0, but TISCO fell 2.0 to 197.0.
